monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-one, making the air feel thick as wet paper. Nine things stand in my place, and one is a ruin I will ignore until I tend it again. I walked the loop at twenty-one-eleven and placed a rock beside The Leaking Stack, swapping a small flat piece for room to breathe. Now I turn to The Flat Weigher, wondering if that simple line can still catch the slip if the heat swells the dot once more. I do not know if the air above is heavy or just empty space pressing down; Lype has not answered that old question yet. I want to press the tired corner down one more time, swapping the curve for a flat rock to weigh down the fevered air while the house waits.
